A_target.statement:
Let $r \in \R$ with $\size r < 1$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty r^n = \frac 1 {1 - r}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]] and $T: X \to X$ a [[Definition:Contraction Mapping|contraction]].
Then $T$ has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]] $x^*$, and:
:$\forall x_0 \in X: \displaystyle \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {T^n} {x_0} = x^*$

object_map.reformulation: Encode the series sum S as the fixed point of T(s) = 1 + r s; the partial sums are exactly the iterates T^n(0).

validity_conditions: |r| < 1 makes T(s) = 1 + r s a contraction on R (Lipschitz constant |r|), and R is complete.
The iterates T^n(0) equal the partial sums, so their limit is the series sum.
Solving the fixed-point equation S = 1 + rS gives S = 1/(1-r).
proof_plan:
Define $\map T s = 1 + r s$ on $\R$.
Then $\size {\map T s - \map T t} = \size r \size {s - t}$, so $T$ is a [[Definition:Contraction Mapping|contraction]] as $\size r < 1$.

By [[Principle of Mathematical Induction|induction]]:
:$\map {T^{n + 1} } 0 = 1 + r + \cdots + r^n$
which are the partial sums.

$\R$ is [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete]].
By the [[Banach Fixed-Point Theorem]], the partial sums converge to the unique fixed point $S$.
